rules.rule: Check for complications after a termination of pregnancy
rules.problem: Type and trigger are right (post-TOP review within 14 days) and every discriminating finding of the page's two questions is listed. Missing: the page's 'Hb < 6' criterion has no finding to check for (no g/dL unit exists, so it cannot be a measurement); add a finding such as (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Hemoglobin below reference range" "finding")) or (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Anemia" "disorder") (qualifier (snomed_concept "Severe (severity modifier)" "qualifier value"))) and consume it in the priority rule.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable ectopic pregnancy after a termination of pregnancy
rules.problem: Diagnosis and 'probable' are right ('ectopic pregnancy likely' in the red box). The evidence is narrower than the page: the red box conditions ectopic only on 'adnexal mass'; closed cervix and small uterus are a parenthetical description in the question line and are anded in as hard requirements. An adnexal mass recorded without both of them would not yield the diagnosis.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable incomplete termination of pregnancy
Urgent: complications within 14 days of a termination of pregnancy
rules.problem: Urgent is justified by the red box ('Manage urgently', 'Refer urgently') and the (and trigger (or ...)) shape is right, but the or-list omits the page's 'Hb < 6' criterion entirely, and adnexal mass is anded with closed cervix and small uterus so an adnexal mass alone does not trigger Urgent although the page lists it as one of the 'any of' items. Minor: the briefing prefers referencing (active_condition "Ectopic pregnancy") from the priority rule where the red box names a likely diagnosis for a subset of criteria, rather than inlining the criteria.

summary: The Urgent priority rule drops one of the page's nine 'any of' criteria, Hb < 6, so a severely anaemic post-TOP patient with normal vitals is not flagged; the language has no g/dL unit, so it needs a finding-based substitute added to the check task and priority rule. The page's parenthetical 'adnexal mass (closed cervix and small uterus)' has been encoded as a three-way and in both the ectopic diagnosis and the priority rule, narrowing both below the page, which conditions ectopic (and urgency) on adnexal mass alone. Everything else, including all SNOMED concepts, the 14-day trigger, the incomplete-TOP or/and structure and the two probable diagnoses, is faithful.
